name: synthetic-devops-fixture
description: Committed CI regression corpus. Entirely synthetic (checkout-api theme); includes near-miss distractors sharing vocabulary with the golden answers so questions are not gimmes. Labels are hand-written, deterministic ground truth.

memories.title: Incident: elasticache-prod connection exhaustion took down checkout
memories.content: 2025-11-03 outage: checkout-api exhausted Redis connections on elasticache-prod during the flash sale. Root cause: no connection pooling, each request opened a fresh client. Resolved by introducing a shared connection pool (max 50) in the redis client wrapper.

memories.title: Connection pool configuration for redis clients
memories.content: After the elasticache-prod incident we standardized redis connection pooling: max 50 connections, 5s acquire timeout, health-check on checkout. Introduced in commit a81f2c. This configuration was later reused by customer-api when they hit the same symptom.

memories.title: customer-api adopted the checkout redis pool settings
memories.content: customer-api saw rising redis latency in staging and adopted the pool configuration from commit a81f2c wholesale (max 50, 5s acquire timeout). Same fix, second service. Pattern: connection exhaustion symptoms should always be checked against pool limits first.

memories.title: checkout-api session storage lives in Redis, app data in PostgreSQL
memories.content: checkout-api stores user sessions in Redis (elasticache-prod) and application data in PostgreSQL (rds-checkout-prod). These are complementary, not redundant: sessions need TTL semantics, orders need transactions.

memories.title: checkout-api listens on port 8080 behind the ALB
memories.content: checkout-api serves HTTP on port 8080; the ALB terminates TLS and forwards to the target group on that port. Health check path is /healthz on the same port.

memories.title: Deploys moved from Jenkins pipelines to GitHub Actions
memories.content: The old Jenkins deploy pipeline for checkout-api was retired in favor of GitHub Actions with OIDC into AWS. The Jenkinsfile is gone; deploys are now .github/workflows/deploy.yml triggered on tag push. Rollback is re-running the workflow with the previous tag.

memories.title: checkout-api requires Python 3.12
memories.content: checkout-api pins Python 3.12 in pyproject.toml; 3.11 fails on the tomllib usage in config loading. CI matrix runs 3.12 only.

memories.title: Evaluated Redis as a response cache and rejected it
memories.content: We considered caching rendered cart responses in Redis but rejected it: invalidation complexity outweighed the latency win at current traffic. Revisit if p99 exceeds 400ms. No connection to the incident work - this was a separate evaluation.

memories.title: PostgreSQL connection pool sizing via pgbouncer
memories.content: rds-checkout-prod sits behind pgbouncer in transaction mode, default pool 20. This is unrelated to the redis pool work; postgres never had an exhaustion incident.

memories.title: ALB idle timeout raised to 120s for report downloads
memories.content: The ALB idle timeout for checkout-api was raised from 60s to 120s because large report downloads were being cut off. Unrelated to port or health-check configuration.

memories.title: checkout-api authenticates requests via short-lived JWTs
memories.content: Every checkout-api request carries a JWT signed by the identity service. Tokens expire after 15 minutes; the client refreshes via the identity service's /token endpoint before expiry. The API validates the signature and expiry on every request, no session lookup needed.

memories.title: JWT signing keys rotate every 90 days
memories.content: The identity service rotates its JWT signing keys every 90 days, publishing the new public key to its JWKS endpoint a week ahead of the switch so checkout-api's cached key set overlaps cleanly. No downtime observed across three rotations so far.

memories.title: New checkout flows ship behind LaunchDarkly flags
memories.content: Every new checkout flow ships behind a LaunchDarkly flag, default off in production. Rollout is staged: internal users, then 5%, 25%, 100%, each held for at least 24h before promoting. This is how the one-click-reorder flow shipped without an incident.

memories.title: Stale checkout flags older than 90 days are auto-archived
memories.content: A cron job archives (does not delete) any LaunchDarkly flag in the checkout-api project untouched for 90+ days, to keep the flag list navigable. Archiving is reversible; deletion is a separate, manual step requiring code review to confirm the flag path is actually dead.

memories.title: checkout-api schema migrations run via Alembic
memories.content: Schema changes for rds-checkout-prod are written as Alembic revisions and applied by the deploy pipeline before traffic cutover to the new version. A failed migration blocks the deploy; the pipeline never promotes a version whose migration didn't apply cleanly.

memories.title: A botched migration once required a manual rollback script
memories.content: In 2025-08 a migration dropped a column still read by an in-flight deploy of the previous version. Recovery required a hand-written rollback SQL script run against production. This predates the current pre-cutover migration gate and is not expected to recur.

memories.title: Checkout submission is rate-limited to 5 requests/min per user
memories.content: checkout-api enforces 5 checkout-submission requests per minute per user via a Redis token bucket keyed on user id. Exceeding the limit returns 429 with a Retry-After header. Limit chosen to stop accidental double-submits without blocking a legitimate retry.

memories.title: Q2 abuse spike prompted the checkout token-bucket limiter
memories.content: A Q2 2025 scripted-abuse spike hammering checkout submission is what originally prompted building a rate limiter. The incident itself resolved once WAF rules blocked the source IPs; the token bucket shipped afterward as a durable safeguard, not as the incident fix.

memories.title: On-call pages when checkout p99 latency exceeds 800ms for 5 minutes
memories.content: A Datadog monitor pages the on-call rotation when checkout-api's p99 latency stays above 800ms for a sustained 5-minute window. Threshold chosen from six months of baseline data; anything shorter than 5 minutes paged on routine traffic blips.

memories.title: Grafana dashboard tracks checkout funnel conversion
memories.content: A separate Grafana dashboard tracks checkout funnel conversion (cart -> submit -> confirm) for product analytics. It is not wired to any alert; nobody gets paged off of it. Distinct from the Datadog latency monitor used for on-call.

memories.title: Always verify an image tag exists before committing a manifest
memories.content: Hard rule: before any commit that sets a container image tag or Helm chart tag, verify the artifact exists in the registry (docker manifest inspect). Learned from a prod outage caused by a typoed tag.

memories.title: PyPI READMEs must use absolute URLs
memories.content: PyPI renders the README standalone, so relative links (LICENSE, docs/foo.md) 404. Always use absolute GitHub URLs in anything published to PyPI.

memories.title: CI that publishes the repo root must exclude tooling dirs
memories.content: Before committing dev tooling (.claude/, hooks, logs) to a repo, check how it publishes. If CI mirrors the repo root to a public target (S3, gh-pages), tooling leaks publicly unless excluded.

memories.title: Terraform S3 backend bootstrap is a chicken-and-egg
memories.content: Terraform cannot manage its own remote state bucket; create the bucket with the CLI before terraform init. Standard bootstrap sequence documented in the platform runbook.

memories.title: Every production incident gets a blameless postmortem within 48 hours
memories.content: Hard rule: any incident that pages on-call gets a written, blameless postmortem within 48 hours, linked from the incident's Slack channel. Late postmortems lose detail fast; the 48-hour window exists because memory of the timeline decays quickly.

memories.title: Rotate a credential that touched a shared channel even if not confirmed leaked
memories.content: Hard rule: if a credential was ever pasted into a shared Slack channel, ticket, or doc - even briefly, even if deleted - rotate it. Do not wait for confirmation that someone actually read it; the cost of rotating is far lower than the cost of guessing wrong.

memories.title: Delete feature flags within 30 days of full rollout
memories.content: Hard rule across all services: once a feature flag reaches 100% rollout and has held for a full deploy cycle, delete the flag and its dead branches within 30 days. Flags left in place past that window are the single biggest source of combinatorial test debt.

memories.title: On-call rotation swaps require 24h notice
memories.content: Anyone swapping an on-call shift with a teammate must post the swap in the on-call calendar at least 24 hours ahead, so paging routes to the right person. Unrelated to postmortems or incident handling itself.

memories.title: billing-service retries a failed invoice charge 3 times with backoff
memories.content: When an invoice charge fails, billing-service retries it 3 times with exponential backoff (1h, 6h, 24h) before flagging the invoice for manual review. Retries stop immediately if the processor returns a hard decline (stolen card, closed account) rather than a soft one.

memories.title: billing-service stores amounts in minor units (cents)
memories.content: All monetary amounts in billing-service are stored as integer cents, never floating-point dollars, to avoid rounding drift across currency conversions and repeated arithmetic. Display formatting to dollars happens only at the API boundary.

memories.title: Stripe webhooks are verified via HMAC signature
memories.content: Every incoming Stripe webhook to billing-service is verified against its HMAC signature header before the payload is processed; unsigned or mismatched requests are rejected with 400. Unrelated to retry logic or currency storage.

memories.title: Dunning emails go out on day 1, 3, and 7 after a failed charge
memories.content: After a charge fails, billing-service's dunning sequence sends emails on day 1, day 3, and day 7, then suspends the subscription if the balance is still unpaid. The schedule is tuned from churn data: shorter gaps drove complaints without recovering more revenue.

memories.title: Sales tax calculation is delegated to a third-party tax API
memories.content: billing-service does not compute sales tax in-house; every invoice line item is sent to a third-party tax API which returns the applicable rate and amount. Unrelated to retry or reconciliation logic.

memories.title: Nightly job reconciles billing-service's ledger against processor settlement
memories.content: A nightly job compares billing-service's internal ledger against the payment processor's settlement report, flagging any invoice whose recorded status doesn't match what actually settled. Discrepancies page a shared billing-ops channel, not on-call.
